title: Destiny (qadar)
hook: Some things you control. Some things you don't. Islam gives you a way to live with both.

screens.text: A job falls through. A friend stops calling. A door opens out of nowhere. *Why did that happen?* Today is about **qadar**, Allah's decree, and how it can bring you peace instead of worry.

**Qadar** is the sixth article of iman: believing in Allah's decree, the good of it and the hard of it [Muslim 8]. Allah knows everything before it happens, it's written, and nothing happens outside His will.
bubbles: *"No disaster strikes except by permission of Allāh. And whoever believes in Allāh - He will guide his heart"* [Q 64:11, Saheeh Intl.].

screens.prompt: Luis has a job interview next week. Which parts are his to do, and which does he hand to Allah?

items.text: Preparing well and showing up on time
items.why: His part. You make real choices, and you're responsible for them.
His part. Asking Allah for help is part of the effort [Muslim 2664].
Allah's part. You're not responsible for an outcome you couldn't control.
Allah's part. People can only do what Allah has already written [Tirmidhi 2516].

screens.text: **But you still choose.** Qadar doesn't make you a puppet. You make real choices, and you're responsible for them. What you're *not* responsible for is the outcome you couldn't control.
bubbles: So you do your part, then trust Allah with the rest. That trust is called **tawakkul**.

options.feedback: Yes [Tirmidhi 2517]. Do your part first, then trust Allah with the rest. That's tawakkul.
Not quite. It's "tie your camel": take the practical step, then trust Allah [Tirmidhi 2517].
Not quite. It's "tie your camel": effort first, then trust [Tirmidhi 2517].

cards.front: "If it's all written, why bother trying?"
cards.back: Your effort is part of what's written. The Prophet ﷺ said: strive for what benefits you, ask Allah for help, and don't give up [Muslim 2664].

cards.front: "Something bad happened. Is Allah angry with me?"
cards.back: Not necessarily. Hard times come to everyone, including the best people. For a believer, patience in hardship is itself good [Muslim 2999].

cards.front: "If only I had done it differently…"
cards.back: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to drop the "if only" and say: Allah decreed, and He does what He wills [Muslim 2664]. Learn the lesson, then let it go.

cards.front: "Can I blame my mistakes on destiny?"
cards.back: No. You chose them, and you can choose to repent. The door back to Allah is always open.

screens.text: **Why this brings peace.** Allah tells us why: *"In order that you not despair over what has eluded you and not exult [in pride] over what He has given you"* [Q 57:23, Saheeh Intl.].
bubbles: What missed you wasn't yours to keep. What reached you was meant for you. You can work hard and still sleep at night.

screens.prompt: Luis doesn't get the job he really wanted. What does tawakkul look like now?

options.text: Make du'a, ask for feedback, keep applying, and trust Allah's plan
options.feedback: Yes. Effort plus trust. He does his part and leaves the outcome to Allah [Tirmidhi 2517].

options.text: Stop applying. If a job is written for him, it'll come
options.feedback: Not quite. Effort is part of the decree. Tie the camel first [Tirmidhi 2517].

options.text: Replay every interview answer for weeks
options.feedback: Not quite. Learn what you can, then drop the "if only" [Muslim 2664]. It's not good for the heart.

screens.text: **When people turn against you.** Some converts lose friends or face family anger. The Prophet ﷺ taught a young companion: if the whole world gathered to help you or harm you, they could only do what Allah had already written [Tirmidhi 2516].
bubbles: People matter, and you stay kind to them. But your life isn't in their hands.

screens.prompt: What's one thing weighing on you right now? Split it in two: what part is in your hands (your effort), and what part you can hand over to Allah (the outcome)?

chips: If Allah already knows everything, do I really have free will?
Why does Allah let bad things happen?
How do I stop worrying about the future?

screens.text: Do your part, then hand it over.
steps: Take one step today on something you've been worrying about
Make a short du'a handing the outcome to Allah
screens.optional_extra: Next time something goes wrong, try replacing "if only" with "Allah decreed, and I'll do my best next time."

screens.text: Allah knows and decrees everything, and you still choose. Do your part, trust Him with the outcome, and drop the "if only."

options.text: Doing your part, then trusting Allah with the outcome
options.feedback: Right. Effort plus trust: tie your camel, then trust Allah [Tirmidhi 2517].

options.text: Doing nothing, because everything is already written
options.feedback: Not quite. Effort is part of the decree. Tawakkul comes after you've done your part.

options.text: Nothing happens outside Allah's knowledge and will, yet people still make real choices
options.feedback: Right. Allah's decree and our responsibility go together [Muslim 8; Q 64:11].

options.text: People have no choices at all
options.feedback: Not quite. We choose and are responsible for our choices, while Allah knows and wills all things.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Belief in the decree, its good and its bad, is the sixth article of iman [Muslim 8].
- Everything is known and recorded by Allah before it happens [Q 57:22]; no disaster strikes except by His permission, and He guides the heart of whoever believes [Q 64:11]. The purpose: not to despair over losses or exult over gains [Q 57:23].
- Humans have real choice and responsibility; tawakkul is effort plus trust [Tirmidhi 2517, hasan].
- Strive for what benefits, seek Allah's help, don't give up, and don't say "if only" after a setback [Muslim 2664].
- If all creation gathered to benefit or harm you, they could do only what Allah had written [Tirmidhi 2516, sahih per al-Albani].
- The believer's affair is all good: gratitude in ease, patience in hardship [Muslim 2999].
- Book background: The Revealed Path ch. 13; Being Muslim a Practical Guide (Divine Decree).

**Likely questions**
- *"Do I have free will?"* Yes, real choice within Allah's knowledge and will. Allah's knowing doesn't force anyone; scholars say the details of how both are true are beyond full human grasp, and we aren't asked to solve it, only to act well and trust. Keep it short; offer the imam for depth.
- *"Why does Allah let bad things happen?"* Acknowledge the pain first. Tests come to everyone; patience is rewarded [Muslim 2999]; this life isn't the whole story (Day 41). Don't explain someone's specific tragedy as punishment.
- *"Does du'a change things?"* Du'a is one of the means Allah has decreed; keep asking. Give the mainstream picture without fine theological debate.
- *"I keep worrying about the future."* Effort plus tawakkul; one step at a time. If worry is constant and heavy, gently mention Day 45 and talking to someone.

**Escalate:** detailed theological debates on predestination and free will; questions about a specific tragedy with religious guilt attached (be gentle, offer the imam).

**Don't**
- Don't use qadar to dismiss pain ("it's just destiny, move on").
- Don't tell anyone a hardship is a punishment for their sins.
- Don't use destiny to excuse harm, abuse or neglect, or to tell someone to stay in danger. Safety rule 6 applies.
